system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Supports inter-node variables (`{agent1Output}`), date/time variables, and custom variables defined directly in the workflow JSON, with optional Jinja2 templating for advanced logic.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompts per node are authored in workflow JSON with variable substitution.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a searchable vector database (keyword search by default, with optional embedding-based semantic/hybrid search)
env_context_strategy.note: Retrieval memory injected; tools (WebFetch, MCP, wiki) can be invoked by nodes.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: a continuously updated "rolling summary" of the entire chat
context_compaction.note: ContextCompactor node also shipped; text_utils reduce_text_to_token_limit truncates.

observation_format.evidence_quote: returns **raw, unformatted data**: either a full string or a generator of data dictionaries
observation_format.note: Image_Processor node handles images from client messages.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Full OpenAI-style tool calling passthrough, including reliable multi-round tool loops through authored-prompt workflows (`appendNativeToolExchange`)
tool_call_format.note: MCP scripts parse JSON from LLM responses.

tool_count.note: Tools are workflow nodes, not a fixed tool list exposed to the model.

edit_primitive.note: No code-editing primitive; SaveCustomFile writes author-specified files.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: connects to an MCP server defined under Public/Configs/MCPServers/ (user-configured) over stdio (local process), SSE, or streamable HTTP, for MCPToolCall nodes
tool_schema_source.note: Non-MCP tool schemas passed through from client / authored JSON.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: mcp 1.28.1 - Model Context Protocol client (MCPToolCall node)

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: WilmerAI processes requests using workflows, which are JSON files that define a sequence of steps (nodes).
loop_primitives.note: Routing chooses a workflow; conditional nodes allow branching.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Instead of relying on unreliable autonomous agents, Wilmer became focused on semi-autonomous Workflows, giving the user granular control of the path the LLMs take
planning_granularity.note: Plan is the human-authored workflow, not agent-generated.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Each node in a workflow can connect to a completely different LLM endpoint or execute a tool.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: execute them as a single, reusable node inside other, larger workflows
delegation_mechanism.note: Sub-workflow nodes hand control to another workflow/LLM persona.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: To the client application, this entire multi-step process appears as a standard API call
human_in_loop.note: No approval gating in the node execution loop.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The architecture is centered on the **`$ExecutionContext$`** object. This data structure encapsulates all runtime information for a single operational step

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: a chronological summary file, a continuously updated "rolling summary" of the entire chat, a searchable vector database

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Manages short-term and long-term memory using a `discussionId` to track conversational context.
state_persistence.note: Memory files persist across calls; no documented mid-workflow resume.

self_verification.evidence_quote: WilmerAI does not track token usage, does not report accurate token usage via its API
self_verification.note: No harness-enforced verification; authors can add LLM-review nodes.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The `$WorkflowProcessor$` iterates through each node in the workflow configuration.
retry_policy.note: No task-level retry in the loop; LLM API failover tests exist.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: designated as either a **responder** (its output is sent to the user) or a **non-responder**
termination_condition.note: Run ends when the workflow node list is exhausted/responder returns; early_termination_exception exists.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: WilmerAI does not track token usage, does not report accurate token usage via its API, nor offer any viable way to monitor token usage.
cost_controls.note: Node-level model choice is author-configured, not cost routing.

timeouts.evidence_quote: requests.request() to the URL set on a WebFetch node (user-authored); optional HTTP/SOCKS proxy. TLS verification is on by default.
timeouts.note: Per-node request timeouts inferred; no run-level timeout documented.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: PythonModule workflow nodes execute user-provided Python scripts from the configured scripts directory with the full privileges of the Wilmer process. These scripts are not sandboxed or validated by Wilmer.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: with the full privileges of the Wilmer process. These scripts are not sandboxed or validated by Wilmer.

network_policy.evidence_quote: The WebFetch and CurlCommand nodes additionally support an opt-in SSRF guard (blockPrivateAddresses / allowedHosts) that can restrict which hosts they are allowed to reach.

permission_model.evidence_quote: These scripts are not sandboxed or validated by Wilmer.

tracing.evidence_quote: At DEBUG level, logs may contain full prompts and LLM responses unless redactLogOutput or encryptUsingApiKey is enabled in the user configuration.
tracing.note: NodeExecutionInfo tracks node metrics used in logging.

replayability.evidence_quote: No telemetry, analytics, phone-home, auto-update, or hardcoded external URLs were found.
replayability.note: No replay facility found in the documented architecture.

eval_hooks.note: Only unit tests; no benchmark evaluation runner.

guardrails.evidence_quote: all log statements that could contain user content are automatically redacted
guardrails.note: SSRF guard blockPrivateAddresses/allowedHosts is the action policy; both opt-in.

target_domain.evidence_quote: WilmerAI is an application designed for advanced semantic prompt routing and complex task orchestration.
target_domain.note: WebFetch/wiki tools and MCP tool use.

open_source.evidence_quote: This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: It connects to various LLM backends (OpenAI, Ollama, KoboldCpp) using a simple configuration system of **Endpoints** (the address), **API Types** (the schema/driver), and **Presets**

first_release_date.note: No release/tag date available in evidence; copyright start year 2024 used as weak basis.
